what_landed: Every damage event whose mitigation site knows the resistance it applied now states it as `resistance_met`, read through one home: `fight/resists._resistance_met_fields`, beside `_mitigate` and off the same class dispatch and the same two arguments, so the field cannot name a resistance the mitigation did not apply. The sites are the rotation's cast parts (the per-hit `ability_mr` its own `_mitigate_hits` was handed), the swing and converted-auto and double-shot rows in fight/autos/simulation.py, every `_swing_event_row` caller in fight/autos/on_hit_layering.py, and the spellblade, true-conversion and doubled on-hit rows in fight/autos/spellblade.py. `fight/ledger/event_rows._damage_event_row` plumbs the field the way it already plumbs `raw_damage`, and `fight/ledger/trace.py` reads it ahead of the declaration's `effective_resistance`. True damage states nothing, because it meets nothing, and the trace prints a blank there rather than a refusal.

landed_against.rule: R-17: this slice declares no diff paths because it moves none. The field is engine-internal: no allow list publishes it, so neither baseline can see it.

why_no_leaf_moves.pair: public_response._public_damage_event enumerates the keys a published damage event carries and `resistance_met` is not among them, so the pair snapshot's serialized fights are byte-identical.
why_no_leaf_moves.coupled: program/views/receipt.py's `_damage_event_rows` publishes an enumerated leaf set (time, target, source, damage_type, damage, raw_damage, pair_damage, overkill, ...) and carries no `resistance_met` leaf, so the coupled receipt is unchanged. Measured: `compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json` reports the same 543 paths after this slice as before it, all of them declared by the two sibling receipts.
why_no_leaf_moves.consequence: Publishing the column is a separate ruling. It would add one leaf per damage event to every coupled scenario, which moves the coupled golden's leaf count and its shape counters, and the step 2 design reserves any addition to a published allow list to the orchestrator.

what_the_fixture_pins.reading: The fight publishes effective armor and MR of 75.3333, which is the post-shred figure. Kog'Maw Q is priced against the 100 magic resistance it goes on to shred, and BOTH of its casts meet 100, not only the one at t=0: `ability_rotation` binds `ability_mr` once per ability row, before `_apply_target_shred` runs, so the shred never boosts the ability that applied it at any cast. Measured, not assumed. `raw * 100 / (100 + resistance_met) == mitigated` holds on all 30 lines.

what_still_refuses_a_resistance.reading: Neither is a mitigation site that forgot to stamp. Cinderbloom takes a share of an already mitigated packet and passes through no mitigation of its own: fight/after/reprice.py imports no _mitigate at all, so there is no resistance it met, which is the shape an amplifier line already states nothing for. A coarse ability row (Ahri W and R) publishes no per-hit events, so the packet the ledger synthesizes for it never passed a mitigation site this trace can read one off. tests/test_fight_trace.py's TestABlankColumn pins both sets over the whole corpus, so a family that stops stating a fact names itself.
what_still_refuses_a_resistance.the_deferred_clone: participant_timeline clones a packet with `{**event}` and re-types it as true damage, so the tick inherits a `resistance_met` its own class cannot have. Stripping it there costs a line in a file whose file-length baseline it already sits exactly on, and the only zero-growth form replaces the spread with an unexplained dict comprehension in a per-tick loop. So the rule has one home instead: fight/ledger/trace._packet_line reads a resistance only for a class that meets one, whatever the event states.

what_did_not_move.claim: No number the engine computes moved. Every stated resistance is the value its own mitigation was handed, carried onto the event rather than recomputed.
evidence: scripts/golden_baseline.json: `python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json` reports 'snapshot identical'.

scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json: `compare` reports 543 differences, every one of them declared by expected-golden-diff-navigability-step2-secondary-delivery.json or expected-golden-diff-navigability-step2-raw-damage.json, and zero extra.
